headline: Anthropic priced the largest IPO on record at $83 and global chip stocks rallied into its debut, but Nvidia fell on its beat-and-raise and the Semis ETF is still -9.3% on five days, so the tape has not yet confirmed the AI earnings.
regime: Wednesday's close was a stalemate: S&P -0.2%, Nasdaq +0.4%, Semis ETF -0.1% (-9.3% on five days, -16.2% on the month), VIX 22.0 (-10.4% on the day but +17.6% on five). Nvidia's record print did not change the narrative (519c0d0233f8); Anthropic's record IPO lifted futures and chips overseas (5ddb3341f176, 9eceb81c90d6). Inside AI only cooling is up on five days (+6.1%, MOD +29.3%); power_nuclear fell again (-1.5%, -11.1% on five) and neoclouds are -13.7% on five. The 10-year at 5.07% still caps multiples.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Modexus investor day sets new long-term targets, most revenue now data centres (454db59864d5, f79142b406b8); cooling +6.1% on five days, MOD +29.3%
nVent shows 4GW+ of deployed liquid cooling and a 2.3MW CDU at SC26 (9c23bb96b1fb); Cramer list: server start dates depend on when the utility delivers power (311834eb44fb)
GE Vernova raised its year-end gas turbine goal to 130GW (536bea878b9a); Capital Group opened a $176m Constellation position (4584fd21ea43); POWL +6.3% on five days
Against: SoftBank took a $3.7bn loss cancelling 13GW of turbines (52246e99036f); power_nuclear -11.1% on five days, SMR -25.2%; a $6.9bn fund sold all its Vistra (0e687497d94f)
theses.change_note: -2: cooling order evidence keeps strengthening, but SoftBank cancelling 13GW of turbines is the first hard sign that power commitments can be unwound, and power stocks keep falling.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Anthropic raised a record ~$81bn at its IPO (c0b1bad6b1fd, 4632852cddb6) and its spending plan lifted AI cloud stocks (2ad8c09fad83)

Broadcom guides AI revenue to ~$115bn in fiscal 2027 (ff003f038d7a); SpaceX funds most of a 10GW build from cash flow (7733e3026f4c); Morgan Stanley sees $1.6tn AI capex from 8 firms in 2027 (d61f95f8b023)
Dell backlog 'keeps inflating' (1aea01ed95fd); Everpure beat (c5cbe393a371)
Against: Nvidia fell on its record print (519c0d0233f8); Nebius cut 2026 guidance on third-party data-centre delays (19dcb95b3de2), i.e. supply-side, not demand
theses.change_note: Anthropic's raise adds funded demand, but Nvidia trading down on the beat shows the market is not paying for it yet; held at 71.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave co-founder bought $30m of bonds after selling $1.2bn+ of stock (60a0e6fe0fed, 52a94e2241dd); floating-rate funds now buying CoreWeave debt (dd50150a0843)
Nebius cut its 2026 revenue range to $3.0-3.2bn on data-centre delays (19dcb95b3de2); NBIS -30.9% on five days; segment -13.7%
Quality gate still drops CRWV, NBIS, IREN, CORZ, CIFR, WULF, APLD
Against: neoclouds rose ahead of the Anthropic debut (2ad8c09fad83)
theses.change_note: +1: an insider choosing the bonds over the stock and a Nebius guide-down are credit-style signals; the Anthropic bounce was one day.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: MU at ~3.4x forward earnings with 75% operating margin and revenue +379%, 44% off its high (shortlist); 'may be 16% undervalued' on AI supply news (f6c1d7b65bcf)
Seagate launches an AI-oriented drive platform (c992c16f61f9); memory +1.0% on the day
Against: MU -40% from its peak 'as cracks appear in the AI boom' (76133bfdc6a3); ETFs net sellers of MU (f8c2a5627654); segment -20.7% on the month
theses.change_note: +3: a 3.4x forward P/E with a 4% FCF yield is a Buffett-style margin of safety if earnings only halve; price still gives no confirmation.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Morgan Stanley: 8 companies to spend $1.6tn on AI infrastructure in 2027 (d61f95f8b023)
Alphabet down 30% (94c57604297a) and giving Gemini Tasks away free against Anthropic (efc3aa1dd67f); ORCL -11.3% on five days and fails the quality gate
Against: SpaceX says cash flow funds most of its build (7733e3026f4c); AMZN +0.6% on five days
theses.change_note: +1: free AI as a competitive weapon means more spend with less pricing power.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: Nvidia fell despite rock-solid earnings (519c0d0233f8); ECB warns AI mega-IPOs could echo past credit bubbles (57d514591a64)
Leveraged and sector ETFs sold across the board on Nov 17 (9fee92d00f82, afa5aa14ef93, 103c257a48f4); Klement sold all his stocks (6a0338a89bcf)
10-year 5.07%, VIX +17.6% on five days; Semis ETF -16.2% on the month
Against: Anthropic's record IPO cleared, showing deep appetite for AI paper (5ddb3341f176)
theses.change_note: The IPO shows demand for new AI supply, which is itself a crowding sign; held.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Texas resumes data-centre approvals weeks before a new government that plans to halt all approvals (8b2907c03e09)
Washington drafting limits on Chinese optical transceiver imports for data centres (ca37f379d1bb)
theses.change_note: +2: first concrete report of an incoming government planning to halt data-centre approvals.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked' retail commentary (73469958e18e); Nvidia fell after its print (519c0d0233f8)
Against: no new probe or export news today; Nvidia's 13F shows it still funding the ecosystem (60357cd62d41)
theses.change_note: -3: no new governance or export news; the thesis now survives mostly on carry-forward and the stock's failure to rally.

compute.note: +0.7% on the day but -7.7% on five; NVDA fell on its beat, AVGO +2.6%.

foundry_equipment.note: -9.8% on five days, TSM -12.3%; quality intact, price now 26% off highs.

memory_storage.note: -20.7% on the month; MU at 3.4x forward is the cheapest quality in the universe.

networking_optical.note: -11.9% on five days, AAOI -27% on a $550m offering; ANET held up.

servers.note: -9.9% on five days, SMCI -19.9%; Dell backlog strong but margins thin.

power_nuclear.note: -11.1% on five days; SoftBank turbine cancellation hurts, stay in cash-generative IPPs.

grid_electrical.note: -4.2% on five days, POWL +6.3%; steadiest bottleneck.

cooling_thermal.note: Only segment up on five days (+6.1%); MOD +29.3% on investor day.

datacenter_neocloud.note: -13.7% on five days; insider buys bonds not stock, Nebius guides down.

hyperscalers.note: -3.8% on five days; Alphabet -30%, free AI pressures pricing.

ai_software.note: +1.8% on the day, -20% on the month; Anthropic listing competes for the same money.

risks: Anthropic trades below its $83 offer and the AI IPO window shuts, hitting sentiment across the chain.
More power-equipment cancellations like SoftBank's 13GW unwind the bottleneck trade's order books.
A 5%+ 10-year and further Fed hikes keep compressing multiples even as AI earnings rise.
An incoming government halting data-centre approvals slows the build-out.
Neocloud credit stress spreads from equity to bonds.
watch: ANT's first-day close versus the $83 offer, and whether software and neoclouds follow it.
Whether NVDA and the Semis ETF hold above Wednesday's lows after the failed post-earnings rally.
GEV and power_nuclear reaction to the SoftBank turbine cancellation.
MU and memory after Sandisk's split today.
